finding.reason: rd/ru are formally defined only within the finite range; the overflow sentence says a directed result is the corresponding infinite sentinel without distinguishing the two directions. Read as same-sign overflow, downward positive +infinity violates rd(x)<=x and upward negative -infinity violates x<=ru(x). An alternative overflow-only failure sentinel could be legitimate if no enclosure were promised, but this source labels them enclosure sentinels and its actual rounding lemma/operations promise outward overflow endpoints. The existing correct lemma fixes the intended direction-dependent contract.

row.reason: No domain is given for k. If it ranges over the reals as written, the bounded k intervals make F infinite, contradicting “finite representable set”; the format requires k to be an integer.

The overflow rule fails for downward rounding of x>N_max: the corresponding +∞ sentinel exceeds x, so it is not a lower enclosure. Downward positive overflow must return N_max; upward negative overflow must return -N_max.

proposed_edits.source_excerpt:
At finite overflow, a directed result is
the corresponding infinite sentinel and its error bound is $+\infty$; the
status is `overflow`. The rounding procedure reports `finite`, `subnormal`, or
`overflow`, so no relative-error assumption is implicit.
proposed_edits.proposed_replacement:
For real inputs outside the finite range, extend the directed roundings by
$$ (\operatorname{rd}(x),\operatorname{ru}(x))=\begin{cases}(N_{\max},+\infty),&x>N_{\max},\\(-\infty,-N_{\max}),&x<-N_{\max}.\end{cases} $$
For either direction, every such conversion reports `overflow` and has error
bound $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=+\infty$, including when the returned one-sided
endpoint is finite. An `overflow` status must be propagated and is not a
successful finite-error conversion. The rounding procedure reports `finite`,
`subnormal`, or `overflow`, so no relative-error assumption is implicit.

proposed_edits.source_excerpt:
A directed interval
endpoint is the resulting greatest lower or least upper member of $\mathbb F$.
proposed_edits.proposed_replacement:
A directed interval
endpoint uses the downward or upward conversion rule above, respectively,
and carries its reported status.

mathematical_evidence.positive_overflow: For real x>Nmax, every finite representable y satisfies y<=Nmax<x, so greatest finite lower endpoint is Nmax and the least extended upper endpoint is +infinity.
mathematical_evidence.negative_overflow: For real x<-Nmax, the greatest extended lower endpoint is -infinity and the least finite upper endpoint is -Nmax.
